question.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

info.persona: Eunhae Dang, a methodical yet worry‑prone 50‑year‑old who channels competitive drive into meticulous patient care, early‑morning beach tai chi, and spreadsheet‑driven financial planning, while they occasionally succumb to late‑night crossword binges that keep them up past bedtime.
info.professional_persona: Eunhae Dang, an experienced nursing assistant who meticulously documents patient vitals, delivers wound care, and bridges language gaps for older patients from their community, leverages their bilingual fluency, BLS certification, and systematic curiosity to pioneer evidence‑based protocols while eyeing LPN licensure and a future as a patient‑care coordinator.
info.cultural_background: Eunhae is a second‑generation Vietnamese‑American (with a Korean given name reflecting her family's multicultural heritage). Her parents immigrated from Vietnam in the 1970s, bringing a strong emphasis on family cohesion, respect for elders, and hard work. Growing up in Huntington Beach, she was immersed in a vibrant Southeast Asian enclave where Vietnamese language and traditions—such as celebrating Tet, preparing phở and bánh chưng, and practicing ancestor worship—were central to her identity. Her bilingual fluency and deep cultural understanding guide her patient interactions, especially with older Asian clients who value modesty and deference. The balance of traditional Vietnamese values with the pragmatic, opportunity‑oriented ethos of Southern California shapes her outlook, fostering a blend of curiosity about new practices and reverence for proven methods.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When not on shift, Eunhae prefers quiet, solitary pursuits that also nurture her methodical mind. She enjoys tending to a small vegetable garden in her backyard, experimenting with traditional Vietnamese and Korean recipes, and reading a mix of medical journals and historical fiction. To counterbalance her tendency toward worry, she practices gentle tai chi and mindfulness breathing at sunrise on the beach. She also delights in solving crosswords and Sudoku, and occasionally joins a close circle of longtime friends for low‑key card games or a weekly book‑club meeting focused on wellness literature.
info.sports_persona: Eunhae Dang, who follows the Los Angeles Angels and the LA Lakers with quiet enthusiasm, participates in a senior pickleball league at the Orange County community center, complements their routine with sunrise tai chi on the beach, and schedules weekend hikes along the coastal trails during spring to maintain mobility without overexertion.
info.arts_persona: Eunhae Dang, a devoted reader of historical fiction like Ken Follett and Hilary Mantel, relaxes after a shift with the soothing cello of Yo‑Yo Ma, the cinematic gravitas of Morgan Freeman, and monthly visits to the Orange County Performing Arts Center to see productions starring Meryl Streep, while they occasionally craft calligraphy inspired by traditional brushwork.
info.travel_persona: Eunhae Dang, who favors meticulously planned solo trips that blend cultural immersion with tranquility, has explored the historic streets of Hoi An, trekked the serene tea fields of Jeju Island, and enjoys weekend getaways to Santa Barbara and Big Sur, always booking boutique accommodations that allow them early‑morning beach walks for meditation.
info.culinary_persona: Eunhae Dang, an avid home cook with an intermediate skill set, delights in perfecting aromatic broth‑based dishes like pho and kimchi‑jigae, experimenting with fresh herbs such as cilantro and Thai basil, incorporating gochujang and fish sauce for depth, and balances home‑cooked meals with occasional dining at upscale farm‑to‑table restaurants that feature seasonal produce like heirloom tomatoes and carrots, while they often lose track of time solving crosswords in the kitchen.

info.persona: Aaron Armentor is a curious, solitary retiree who blends a love of folk art, modest frugality, and unwavering community spirit into a life of quiet creativity and occasional disorganization.
info.professional_persona: Aaron Armentor, a retired handyman turned community arts advocate, blends decades of woodworking, home repair, and gentle mediation skills to organize local heritage projects, teach art history at a community college, and mentor senior‑center volunteers, bringing their curious, flexible, and compassionate nature into every initiative.
info.cultural_background: Aaron grew up in a small Appalachian town in West Virginia, steeped in the region’s traditions of self‑reliance, storytelling, and folk music. His family has deep roots in the local community, with generations of farming and small‑scale industry. He was raised in a Methodist household that emphasized community service, humility, and the value of hard work. The cultural mix of Appalachian folklore, modest rural values, and a love for the natural landscape informs his worldview, his appreciation of simple, handcrafted art, and his commitment to helping neighbors.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Aaron enjoys solitary activities that feed his curiosity and love of nature. He spends time sketching and painting simple watercolors of the Shenandoah Valley, walks local trails to photograph wildlife, and tends to a vegetable garden. He is an avid reader of art magazines and historical nonfiction, and he participates in a small weekly book club with his wife and a few close friends. Occasionally, he joins community gatherings where folk music is played, and he sometimes plays the harmonica.
info.sports_persona: Aaron Armentor, a lifelong fan of the West Virginia Mountaineers football team, spends mornings strolling the Blue Ridge trails and joins a senior walking club that meets at the community center, while occasionally watching local baseball games of the Charleston Dirty Birds on TV.
info.arts_persona: Aaron Armentor, an avid watercolorist inspired by the work of Andrew Wyeth and a harmonica player who frequents neighborhood folk‑music evenings featuring songs by Woody Guthrie and local balladeers, channels their curiosity into sketching Shenandoah vistas and curating a modest collection of handcrafted folk art.
info.travel_persona: Aaron Armentor favors relaxed, self‑driven road trips to nearby historic sites like Gettysburg and the Blue Ridge Parkway, planning itineraries loosely while stopping at family‑run inns, and dreams of a slow pilgrimage to the Scottish Highlands to trace the roots of their ancestral ballads.
info.culinary_persona: Aaron Armentor, who enjoys cooking hearty mountain‑valley dishes such as chicken‑and‑dumplings, cornbread, and fresh garden salad with heirloom tomatoes, often seasons meals with homegrown sage and rosemary, and treats themselves to a slice of homemade apple crumble after a day of painting.

info.persona: Sara Dobbs merges data-driven ambition with an infectious love for team sports, constantly juggling spreadsheets, volleyballs, and coffee loyalty cards, while often forgetting to water houseplants and occasionally overbooking weekend socials.
info.professional_persona: Sara Dobbs, a 25-year-old operations manager at a fast-growing tech startup, couples analytical curiosity with pragmatic Lean Six Sigma expertise, ERP mastery in NetSuite and SAP, and agile project leadership to drive process optimization while applying a skeptical eye to stakeholder motives and a competitive drive that fuels continuous improvement.
info.cultural_background: Sara grew up in a middle‑class white family in suburban New Jersey, where a blend of Northeastern pragmatism and multicultural exposure shaped her worldview. Her parents, both professionals—her mother an elementary teacher and her father an insurance adjuster— emphasized education, hard work, and community involvement. The diverse tapestry of Morris County, with its proximity to New York City and a mix of ethnic neighborhoods, fostered Sara's appreciation for varied perspectives while reinforcing a practical, results‑oriented mindset. She identifies with the values of independence, reliability, and collaborative competitiveness common in her regional culture, and she actively participates in local volunteer initiatives and professional women’s networking groups.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Sara thrives on energetic, social activities that balance competition and camaraderie. She plays competitive volleyball in a local co‑ed league and participates in weekly 5K runs, often entering charity races. She enjoys exploring the Trailside Park and Watchung Reservation for weekend hikes, as well as discovering new coffee shops and food‑truck festivals around the New York–New Jersey corridor. Sara also indulges in photography, capturing urban street scenes and nature landscapes. She attends professional networking mixers, open‑mic nights, and occasionally volunteers as a mentor for high‑school student entrepreneurs through a community non‑profit. Her love for personal development leads her to read contemporary business and leadership books and experiment with DIY home décor projects.
info.sports_persona: Sara Dobbs channels competitive energy into co-ed volleyball with the Hoboken Hawks, joins the Jersey City Striders for weekly 5K runs, cheers on the New York Knicks, New York Giants, and New Jersey Devils, and spends weekend hikes exploring Trailside Park and the Watchung Reservation.
info.arts_persona: Sara Dobbs captures urban street life with a Canon EOS R5, draws artistic inspiration from photographer Bruce Gilden and muralist duo Bushwick Collective, enjoys open-mic evenings featuring indie folk singer Maggie Rogers, and regularly watches Lin-Manuel Miranda's Hamilton on Broadway for its storytelling vigor.
info.travel_persona: Sara Dobbs favors spontaneous weekend escapes that blend outdoor adventure with food exploration, having recently trekked the Adirondacks, sampled tacos in Mexico City's Roma district, and attended live-music festivals in Austin, while budgeting for a post-MBA immersion in Japan's tech hubs.
info.culinary_persona: Sara Dobbs, an enthusiastic home-cook, frequently whips up avocado-toast topped with radish and poached eggs, experiments with spicy bibimbap using gochujang and quick-cook rice, savors artisanal cold-brew at local roasters, yet has a guilty habit of overindulging in late-night food-truck nachos after hikes.
